_note: Eight buyers and all twenty-eight of their pairs, which is C(8,2) and complete — `every_pair_is_authored` counts it. A buyer wants two grids and has a floor; two kin in a row leave a **bargain**, and three of the twenty-eight leave an ench that nothing in the game sells. Those three are the Stall's own, held back from M21.6 until there was a counter to get them from.

buyers.name: The Shift Foreman
buyers.blurb: He buys for eleven other people and none of them is here. He has a list and he will not show you the list.

buyers.name: The Under-Clerk
buyers.blurb: She writes down what she paid and then writes down what she should have paid, in a different column, in a different hand.

buyers.name: The Rind Cutter
buyers.blurb: Buys nothing he cannot carry and carries a great deal. He has been doing this since before the works was the works.

buyers.name: The Tenth Surveyor's Boy
buyers.blurb: He is not a boy and he was not the tenth surveyor's. He is very particular about the second part.

buyers.name: The Quench Hand
buyers.blurb: Comes in wet, leaves wet, and pays in coins that are warm. Nobody has asked about the coins.

buyers.name: The Woman From High Wick
buyers.blurb: She says High Wick as though you have been. Nobody has been. She buys the strange things and she buys them quickly.

buyers.name: The Drover
buyers.blurb: Buys on the way through and never on the way back, which everybody has noticed and nobody has explained.

buyers.name: Nine of Ashes' Cousin
buyers.blurb: Says it like a job title. Pays like one too, and does not haggle, and does not look at what they are buying.

kin.blurb: Two of them in a row, and the second one leaves something on the counter that was not for sale.
